blogs.title: When Hyponatremia Meets Headache: Unmasking Neuro-Behçet's via SIADH
blogs.description: Explore the critical diagnostic pitfall where Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuretic Hormone Secretion (SIADH) serves as the presenting sign of acute neurological Behçet's disease. This post discusses why clinicians must suspect CNS inflammation in patients with mucocutaneous ulcers and unexplained hyponatremia, even when brain MRI is initially normal.

blogs.title: The Normal MRI Trap: Diagnosing Acute Parenchymal Neuro-Behçet's Without Radiographic Evidence
blogs.description: Challenge the reliance on structural imaging in neuro-inflammation. This article analyzes the case where acute neuro-Behçet's presented with meningoencephalitis symptoms but a completely normal MRI, emphasizing the necessity of interpreting CSF findings (aseptic meningitis) alongside clinical mucocutaneous criteria for timely diagnosis.

blogs.title: Beyond Steroids: Can Colchicine Monotherapy Treat Acute Neuro-Behçet's and Associated SIADH?
blogs.description: Discuss the controversial role of colchicine in acute neurological involvement. While guidelines favor high-dose steroids, this post examines the evidence from this case where colchicine alone resolved mucocutaneous, neurological, and endocrine symptoms, questioning current treatment algorithms for early-phase neuro-Behçet's.

blogs.title: Persistent Hiccups and Rhabdomyolysis: The Underappreciated Clues of Severe Hyponatremia
blogs.description: Highlight two often-overlooked clinical markers of profound hyponatremia: intractable hiccups and rhabdomyolysis. This post connects these seemingly unrelated symptoms to the underlying electrolyte disturbance driven by CNS inflammation, urging clinicians to check creatine kinase and monitor for diaphragmatic irritability in confused or febrile patients.

blogs.title: The Diagnostic Dilemma: Concurrent Systemic and Neurological Onset in Behçet's Disease
blogs.description: Address the rarity of simultaneous presentation of systemic Behçet's and acute neuro-Behçet's, which typically manifests years later. This blog breaks down the differential diagnosis strategy when a patient presents with fever, ulcers, and CNS symptoms, focusing on how to distinguish this entity from viral meningoencephalitis, sarcoidosis, and malignancy without over-testing.
